entries.english: The 22 Mweru Geographical Sub-Tribes, 13 Mwiria Totemic Clans (Netiri) & Ntowaita Exodus Legend (Hobley 1910, pp. 156–158)
entries.translation: 22 Mweru Sub-Tribes & Chiefs (p. 156): (1) Janjai (Kamuru), (2) Oringo (Njoo), (3) Kunati (Waikaiwa), (4) Mbuya (Waivori), (5) Akithii (Mutwiarando), (6) Athwana (Kirigwa), (7) Muthara (Ndaminuki), (8) Karama, (9) Iembe (Kiliungu), (10) Muchi Muguru (Njaiili), (11) Kithio (Mutiarando), (12) Amwa, (13) Mnithu (Paimwisu), (14) Nyangini, (15) Tera, (16) Ntagira, (17) Karuanjoi, (18) Kithironi, (19) Rukho, (20) Iokhi, (21) Amengñendi, (22) Thaicho (Paratobi) • 13 Mwiria Clans & Netiri Totems (p. 157): (1) Ntowaita (dominant clan, formerly Njiru), (2) Athanya (vyondo basket twine), (3) Njaru (white cattle), (4) Nthia (speckled cattle), (5) Ntuni (red cattle), (6) Amakui (edible root Mukui), (7) Athinga (giraffe), (8) Antuanthama (mpala; antu = people), (9) Singamburi (goats), (10) Antwa mwakia ('greedy people', dik-dik), (11) Angilo (black cattle), (12) Mwianda (lice; anda = louse), (13) Amatu (francolin; matu = ears) • Ntowaita ('ku-ita' = to cut) Exodus Legend (pp. 157–158): Their laibon solved 3 enemy tests (fleas from chopped tail-hair, two-sided hairy sandals from donkey ears, and an iron rod from earth to sky by inspecting a volunteer's entrails) and parted the river waters after pouring ewe/ass/human milk into the river
entries.pronunciation: mwi-ri-a / ne-ti-ri / nto-wai-ta / ku-i-ta / jan-jai / o-rin-go / mu-tha-ra / i-em-be
entries.context: C. W. Hobley (1910) 'Ethnology of A-Kamba and Other East African Tribes', Part II, Ch. VI, pp. 156–158

entries.english: The 14 Tharaka (Thaka) Clans (Mwiriga / Mbai) & Totems (Nthuku) Recorded by C. W. Hobley (1910 Appendix 6, p. 169)
entries.translation: Ntonga (Duiker nthia), Mbua (Baboon Ikuli), Koli (Monkey ntheo), Nya (Aardvark guma), Nkuyu (Dik-dik Kabii), Kamowao (Hartebeest Ando), Kanyaki (Elephant nzoo), Kangina (Wart-hog ngi), Kamugwi (Reedbuck ndoya), Kathoka (Bush-pig ngulwe), Kanjogo (Elephant nzoo), Engimu (Rhino ngimo), Kirundu (Buffalo mbogo), Mutua (Hyaena mbiti); Thaka wizard = Mugao vs. medicine man = Mutu muwao (p. 93 n.), spirit tamarind shrine = Mthumuba (p. 85 n.)
entries.pronunciation: mwi-ri-ga / nthu-ku / nton-ga / m-bu-a / ko-li / ka-nya-ki / ki-run-du
entries.context: C. W. Hobley (1910) 'Ethnology of A-Kamba and Other East African Tribes', p. 2, pp. 85, 93 & Appendix (6), p. 169

entries.english: Mount Kenya Dialect Variants in Johnston (1919, Vol. I, pp. 98–112 #11 E. Embu, C. Cuka, Mw. Mwimbe, M. Meru #11a, Emb. Emberre, Þ. Þeraka, Ig. Igωji)
entries.translation: Dialectal Variants Recorded by Johnston (pp. 98–106): Mū-kω (white ant/termite, Embu), M-buta (back, Cuka), Ki-ai pl. ci- (man's breast, Embu) / Ru-ria pl. n-dia (Meru) / Ru-gωnω (Mwimbe), Mū-rata (brother, Meru/Mwimbe), N-jamba (bull, Cuka/Meru), Rū-sena (country, Meru), Mu-tinjire (doctor/diviner, Embu/Meru), Ṅ-giti (dog, Meru/Embu), Mū-raṅgω (door, Meru), A-va (father, Embu) / Ba-va (father/grandfather, Meru) / Ūma (grandfather, Embu), G-itigirra (fear, Meru) / Ṅ-korora (fear, Mwimbe), Gi-þaka (forest, Meru), N-kuā (ghost, Meru), Ki-hīa (he-goat, Meru), Mu-ruṅgu (God, Cuka/Embu/Meru), Mū-þiginyω (heel, Embu) / N-tωgigω (Meru) / Ki-soṅua (Mwimbe), Kī-būtū (hoe, Embu) / I-þanwa (hoe, Meru), Gī-þūnω (hut, Embu), M-būta (hunger, Meru), N-gatia (lion, Nyeri/Meru), Mami (mother, Meru), N-jīwa (pigeon, Meru), Kī-gwū/Gωcu (song, Embu) / Mū-ūmba (song, Meru), Kī-rāma (spear, Meru), Siyare (stick, Meru), N-twmōi (tail, Meru), Mā-zigūma (urine, Meru), Rω-e (water, Meru), Mū-gūrra (woman, Meru), Kī-šīī (womb, Meru)
entries.pronunciation: mu-kω / ki-ai / mu-ti-nji-re / gi-bu-tu / gi-thu-nω / ki-gwu
entries.context: Sir Harry H. Johnston, 'A Comparative Study of the Bantu and Semi-Bantu Languages' (Vol. I, 1919, pp. 98–112; Vol. II, 1922, pp. 28–30)
